tagline.text: A half-moon cove of white sand and calm turquoise water at the northern tip of Luzon

location.label: Location
location.text: Sitio Gaoa, Barangay Balaoi, Pagudpud, Ilocos Norte (Maira-ira Point)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500–3,000 (admission, transport, a simple meal and a cottage; per person)

children.text: Blue Lagoon is a half-moon cove at Maira-ira Point on the northern edge of Pagudpud, named for its white sand and turquoise water. You can swim and kayak when the sea is calm, surf when the waves arrive, and there is also a zip line across the cove.

Blue Lagoon is a beach in Pagudpud, the northernmost town in Ilocos Norte, and locals also call it Maira-ira Beach or Malingay Cove. Administratively it is in Sitio Gaoa of Barangay Balaoi, and the cove opens in a half-moon shape between Nacatnagan Cliff and the Dos Hermanos islands. Wikipedia describes Maira-ira Beach as the northernmost tip of Luzon Island, on the Luzon Strait. It is about
from Laoag, the main city of Ilocos Norte (to Pagudpud town), and a drive is said to take 1.5 to 2 hours.

One explanation of the name is that when the sea is calm the water is still as a mirror and reflects the blue of the sky. The sand is white with fine pebbles, and while the shoreline is shorter than that of Saud Beach in Pagudpud, the color of the sea is described as just as stunning. If Saud Beach is wide and good for leisurely swimming, Blue Lagoon is snug inside the cove and has activities such as surfing and a zip line, so it suits more active travelers.

Around the cove are beachfront restaurants, souvenir shops, homestays, cottages and several resorts. The largest accommodation on the beach is said to be Hannah's Resort and Convention Center, which is described as operating a long zip line across the cove. I could not confirm whether the resort still operates, as sources differ. Surf schools are also said to be on the shoreline.

This guide is for travelers making a day trip or an overnight trip from Laoag through Pagudpud. I could not find current official information on admission fees, surf season and road conditions, so I based it on travel sources from 2019 to 2023. Check exact fees and access conditions with the Pagudpud municipal office or the Ilocos Norte tourism office.

Surrounded by Nacatnagan Cliff and the Dos Hermanos islands, the sea is as still as a lake when the waves are small. One travel blog suggests the reflection of the sky in the water is the origin of the name. Go early in the morning for fewer people.
White, finely pebbled sand goes well with turquoise water. Some reviewers compare it to Boracay, though it is described as far quieter. In the strong midday sun, be sure to bring a hat and sunscreen.
When surf waves arrive, you can surf in the shallow cove. One blog says suitable waves come in July–September. Surf schools are said to be on the shoreline, but check names and prices locally.

, said to be operated by Hannah's Resort, is described as crossing the cove. One description says you can look over the whole cove from the launch lookout. I could not confirm whether it operates or its price.
Swimming, snorkeling, kayaking, paddleboarding and banana boat rides are described. One source lists a banana boat at ₱1,800 for five people. Prices differ by operator, so check before you ride.

The Dos Hermanos islands are close to the beach and can reportedly be reached by boat. On the way you also pass Bantay Abot Cave and Timmangtang Rock. Kabigan Falls and the Patapat Viaduct in Pagudpud are easy to add to the same trip.

Beachfront restaurants serve seafood and Ilocano food, and dishes such as bagnet (crispy fried pork), empanada and poqui-poqui (a grilled eggplant dish) are described. Some homestays will cook meals if you ask.
It is described as a good place for sunrise and sunset photos.
Take a bus or van to Pagudpud from the Laoag bus terminal or van terminal. Morning buses are said to be best.
Get off in Pagudpud or Gaoa and take a tricycle to Blue Lagoon.
Pay the entrance fee, walk the beach and take photos.
Enjoy swimming, kayaking or snorkeling, and in surf season look into a surf school.
Have lunch at a beachfront restaurant.
Head to Bantay Abot Cave or Kabigan Falls.
Return to Laoag by bus or van.
Check the last bus times in advance. The unpaved road can be dark after sunset.
Travel from Laoag to Pagudpud and drop your bags at Saud Beach.
Take a tricycle out to Blue Lagoon and back.
Enjoy the sunset and dinner near your lodging.
See Kabigan Falls or the Patapat Viaduct.
See the Bangui windmills and return to Laoag.
The tricycle North Tour package (about ₱600) sometimes includes Blue Lagoon, but fares change.
There are flights from Manila to Laoag International Airport (LAO), and the flight takes about
1 hour
. Airlines and schedules change by season, so check when you book.
By bus, there are buses to Laoag from Cubao or Pasay that take about
10–12 hours
. A 2019 source gives fares of ₱800–980, but check current fares locally.
Wikipedia gives the road distance from Manila to Pagudpud as about
558 km
From the Laoag bus terminal, take a Partas, Fariñas or Maria de Leon bus bound for Claveria or Cagayan to Pagudpud. It is said to take about
1.5–2 hours
Vans to Pagudpud are also said to leave from the van terminal near the Laoag public market.
Get off at Gaoa and take a tricycle to Blue Lagoon, which takes about
15–30 minutes
. A source from the 2010s gave about ₱15 per person from Gaoa to the beach, but this may be very different now.
A direct tricycle from Saud Beach is known to cost about ₱300–500 one way, so bargain before you ride.
After heavy rain the unpaved road can turn to mud and make travel difficult.

One travel blog gives November–May, when the sea is calm, as the good period for swimming and relaxing, and July–September, when the waves arrive, as the good period for surfing. According to Wikipedia, Pagudpud is driest in December (about 2 mm a month), and the wet season peaks in July and August, with more than 470 mm a month. The mean daily high is about

In the rainy season the unpaved road can become muddy and the waves rough, so take care. On holidays and weekends in the high season the beach is crowded, so weekday mornings are quieter. Check the forecast during typhoon season.

items.label: Admission
items.note: Children, seniors and students ₱10 (2019–2023 sources); a May 2026 guide also says about ₱20, but sources range from free to ₱20 and none is official

items.label: Camping
items.note: Tent not included; check permission for the area (2019 source)

Around Blue Lagoon there are homestays, small lodgings, cottages and resorts, and you can stay right on the beach. Sources list Casa Consuelo Resort, Pannzian Beach Resort, Kingfisher Sand Sea Surf Resort, Natsuca Beach Resort and Blue Lagoon Inn and Restaurant. Hannah's Resort and Convention Center is known as a large resort in the area, but I could not confirm whether it is operating now, so check before you book.

Meals are available at beachfront restaurants and food stalls. Seafood, bagnet and empanada are described, and you can also bring your own food or ask a homestay to cook for you. Bring plenty of cash. Only some resorts accept cards.
Bring cash for admission and parking. Parking is described as free, but you have to find a space yourself.
It is best to agree on the tricycle fare for the round trip before you board.
Taking a morning bus gives you a relaxed schedule and makes it easier to secure a ride back.
Bring swimwear, a change of clothes, a waterproof bag, sunscreen, water and snacks. Bringing your own snorkel gear is said to be better.
To avoid the crowded commercial stretches, look for the part of the shore farther from the town center.
Do not take sand from the beach, and carry your trash out.
Videoke noise is reportedly allowed only until 11 pm under a barangay ordinance.
Blue Lagoon is said to be quieter than Saud Beach, but Saud Beach has more room for leisurely swimming. If swimming is your priority, see both before deciding.
The Ilocos Norte tourism office (phone 0908 810 8621) and Casa Consuelo (0998 982 8438) are listed as places to ask.

I found no recent official information on Blue Lagoon's entrance and environmental fees. In July 2026 the Pagudpud municipality said it collects an environmental fee (₱50 for adults and so on) and cottage rates under an ordinance at Saud Beach Park, so ask locally first whether similar fees apply at Blue Lagoon.
Admission is given as ₱15–20 depending on the source, and some sources are old. Check with the municipal office before you go.
When the waves are rough (July–September and so on), swimming can be dangerous, so follow lifeguards and local guidance.
In the rainy season the unpaved road turns muddy, and a tricycle or a four-wheel-drive vehicle may be needed.
I could not confirm whether individual facilities such as Hannah's Resort are operating, or the zip line price.
I could not confirm whether photography and drones are allowed, so follow local guidance.
